subject: Inflight throughput fluctuations: root cause analysis and remediation plan
body:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@quantahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@quantahealth.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed throughput jitter on our reserved pool (examples attached)

Hannah / Redwood team,

We started seeing increased variability in per-request throughput yesterday evening and again this morning across our dedicated pool. Latency spikes are correlated with short bursts of concurrent requests — roughly 200–400ms extra tail for ~6% of requests over the last 12 hours. Attached is a small log snippet showing request IDs and timestamps (qhealth-request-log-snippet.txt).

This is impacting our clinical triage flow (real-time inference) and we need a short-term mitigation and a clear plan for a permanent fix. Can you confirm whether this looks like queueing/preemption jitter on the reserved GPUs or something on our side?

What we need from Redwood:
- A reversible mitigation we can enable quickly (within 24–48 hours).
- A root-cause hypothesis and estimated ETA for a permanent resolution.
- Any temporary credits or SLA accommodation while we triage.

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Sr. Platform Ops
QuantaHealth

----
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@quantahealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed throughput jitter on our reserved pool (examples attached)

Hi Maria — thanks for the logs and the clear summary. We saw the same pattern on our side for your reserved pool between 22:30 UTC and 05:00 UTC.

Quick answers up-front:
1) Short-term mitigation: we can enable a soft-priority lane for your reserved pool to isolate critical request paths and reduce head-of-line blocking. This is reversible and can be applied in a maintenance window within 6 hours.
2) Hypothesis: intermittent KV-cache eviction thrashing combined with aggressive batching during overlapping short-lived spikes. That combination can surface as jitter even when average throughput is within bounds.
3) SLA credits: I can approve a 10% monthly credit for impacted windows while we complete RCA; I'll loop in Finance for formal paperwork.

We will run a root-cause analysis and follow up with an action plan by tomorrow EOD. Karthik / David — can you pick this up and reproduce in staging? I attached a proposed headroom playbook (headroom_playbook_v2.pdf) with the soft-priority lane steps; please review.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

----
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed throughput jitter on our reserved pool (examples attached)

Team — notes from the initial runbook check and a short repro in staging:  

Summary:
- Reproduced ~95th–99th percentile latency spikes when we emulate QH request pattern with overlapping short sessions and enabled aggressive batching.
- Root cause appears to be a pair of interactions: (A) short-lived KV cache churn causing transient cache-miss storms; (B) our batching heuristic temporarily increasing batch size when token distributions align — that increases scheduling latency for some in-flight requests.

Immediate remediation (can ship to prod as a feature flag):
1) Enable "soft-priority lanes" for critical endpoints (routes) to bypass standard batching for small, latency-sensitive requests. This keeps throughput high for bulk requests while trimming tail latency.
2) Reduce the upper bound on batch growth when workload variance is high (adaptive cap).
3) Add a short (250ms) anti-thundering hold on KV eviction for highly contended models in your pool.

Estimated timeline:
- Feature-flag rollout to your reserved pool (non-disruptive): 3–6 hours after sign-off.
- Monitoring & observability: add tracer to collect per-request scheduling metrics and publish a dedicated dashboard (we've attached a draft in the headroom playbook).
- Full permanent fix (kernel optimizations + batching algorithm tuning): 2–3 weeks with an opt-in release.

Action items: Karthik to prepare rollout steps and a maintenance window; Lauren to own customer comms and credits. I created Jira QH-3421 to track.

-David
David Kim
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: headroom_playbook_v2.pdf (draft), qhealth-request-log-snippet.txt (from customer)

----
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@quantahealth.com>, ops@quantahealth.com
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed throughput jitter on our reserved pool (examples attached)

Maria — follow-up and plan of record. Thanks again for the quick log dump; that made repro straightforward.

Planned remediation (requested start: Thu 7 May 20:00 UTC, 2-hour window):
- 20:00 UTC: enable soft-priority lane for your critical model routes (non-disruptive toggle).
- 20:15 UTC: deploy adaptive batch cap and anti-thundering KV hold (feature flagged).
- 20:30–22:00 UTC: monitor 1-min and 5-min p90/p99 latencies and token throughput; we will keep a runbook open and revert flags immediately if any regressions appear.

Temporary accommodations: we will issue a 10% usage credit for May's bill covering the windows where p99 exceeded your SLA during the affected dates. Formal credit paperwork will follow from Finance.

Observability & RCA: we created Jira QH-3421 and a short dashboard (link below) that will be shared with your ops team. The permanent engineering work (kernel path and batching improvements) is scheduled for the 2–3 week cycle following this week; we'll share a changelog and release notes before GA.

Please reply to confirm the maintenance window. If the time doesn't work, propose an alternative 2-hour window tonight or tomorrow morning UTC.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
